title: Have fun watching us bake a red velvet cake

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Hi Grandma! How have you been lately?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Hello, my dear! I'm so happy to be here and bake with you. What are we making today?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm glad you're here too! I was thinking we could make some chocolate chip cookies. They're always a hit!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, baking with love is the best ingredient! What recipe are we going to try today?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I literally just said chocolate chip cookies. Why are you asking again?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I wasn't asking again. My second sentence was still part of my first thought. You talked over it.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I wasn't talking over it. I was answering your question.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You answered while I was still speaking. That's overlapping.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You asked two questions back to back. I answered the first one.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: The second wasn't a question. It was enthusiasm. You cut into my enthusiasm.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I thought you were done. You paused.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I paused for breath. Not for you to correct me.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I wasn't correcting. I was clarifying.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Clarifying that I don't listen. That's a correction.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Okay, forget cookies. Let's do red velvet cake instead.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Red velvet? Where did that come from?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I was about to suggest it when you started talking over my cookie explanation.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I didn't talk over. I was responding to your 'hit' comment.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You responded before I finished my sentence about the cookies.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Your sentence had multiple parts. I thought you reached the end.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: How? I said 'They're always a hit' and then you jumped in.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Because 'hit' sounded like a conclusion. Like you were wrapping up.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It was an observation, not a conclusion. I had more to say.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: How am I supposed to know that? I'm not in your head.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: By waiting one extra second.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: A second of silence feels like an invitation. In my day, we filled silences.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: This isn't your day. This is now. And now, I need you to hear the full plan.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Fine. I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Red velvet cake. We need flour, sugar, cocoa powder, buttermilk, eggs, butter, vanilla, red food coloring, baking powder, and salt.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Baking powder! I was wondering when you'd remember that.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I didn't forget. You interrupted before I got to it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I was agreeing with you. Baking powder is important. That's support, not interruption.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Support doesn't require speaking while I'm listing ingredients.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I got excited. I thought you were done with the list.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I said 'and salt' at the end. That means I was still going.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You said 'and salt' after I spoke. I thought my comment prompted you to remember salt.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Salt was always on the list. Your comment just made me rush.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: So now it's my fault you rushed?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's your fault I couldn't deliver the list at my own pace.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Your pace is too slow. I get bored waiting.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Boredom is better than wrong ingredients.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I haven't put in any wrong ingredients.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Because I stopped you before you could.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: That's insulting.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's preventive.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Preventive of what? My participation?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Preventive of mistakes caused by incomplete information.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You treat me like a child.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I treat you like someone who doesn't understand my pauses.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Your pauses are ambiguous. They feel like endings.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: They're not endings. They're transitions.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: To me, a transition sounds like an opening.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Then we have a fundamental misunderstanding of conversation structure.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Apparently. In my world, overlapping shows engagement. In yours, it shows disrespect.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Not disrespect. Just lack of listening.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I am listening. I just respond quickly.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Before I've finished my thought.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Your thoughts are long. I have thoughts too.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Then wait your turn.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I feel like I'm in school.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm not trying to school you. I'm trying to communicate.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It feels like lecturing.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Because you won't acknowledge the problem.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I acknowledge that we have different styles.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Different styles that don't work together.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: They worked fine when you were little.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: When I was little, I didn't need precise instructions.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: And now you do. Everything has to be precise.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Baking requires precision.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Baking also requires love. And patience.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I have patience. I've been patient for an hour.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: An hour of patience that looks like frustration.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Let's just measure. Two cups of sifted—

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Sifted? I already poured it straight from the bag.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: —flour. I said sifted flour. You didn't let me finish.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You said 'two cups of sifted' and stopped. I thought you were thinking.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I stopped because you reached for the flour bag.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I reached because you paused. It was an awkward silence.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It wasn't awkward. I was reading the recipe.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You should tell me when you're reading. I can't read your mind.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You should wait for me to finish before acting.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You take too long. I was being proactive.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Proactive without full information is just wrong. Now we have unsifted flour.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Does it really matter?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Yes. Sifted flour is lighter. The cake texture depends on it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You didn't explain that. You just said 'sifted.'

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I was about to explain when you cut me off.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I didn't cut you off. I was helping.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Helping requires knowing what to do. You didn't.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Don't be rude. I'm your grandmother.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm not being rude. I'm frustrated because you keep misunderstanding my pauses.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Your pauses are confusing. They feel like invitations to speak.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: They are not invitations. They are thinking breaks.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Well, they feel like endings.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Then we need a signal. When I'm reading, I'll hold up the card. When I'm done, I'll put it down.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: That might work.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Card up. Reading. We need baking powder, salt, buttermilk, two eggs, half a cup butter, vanilla, and red food coloring. Done reading.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Baking powder! I knew you forgot something earlier.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I didn't forget. You interrupted before I got to it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I was just confirming. That's agreement, not interruption.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You said it while I was reading. That breaks the rule.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I thought 'done reading' only applied to the list. I was commenting after.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You commented over my 'done reading.'

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I didn't hear 'done reading.' I was focused on baking powder.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: This is impossible. You hear what you want to hear.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: That's not fair. I'm trying to follow your rules.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The rule is simple. Wait for me to finish.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I thought I was waiting. Your 'done reading' was too quiet.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It wasn't quiet. You were just ready to pounce with your comment.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Pounce? I was being helpful.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Helpful comments after I finish. Not during. Not overlapping.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Fine. I will sit on my hands.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You don't have to sit on your hands. Just listen.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I'm listening. But when you pause, my brain thinks it's my turn.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Your brain needs to learn that pauses aren't turns.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: That's easy for you to say. You've had years of practice.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's not practice. It's basic courtesy.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: In my generation, overlapping was courtesy. It showed you were engaged.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: In my generation, it shows you don't care what the other person is saying.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: We care differently.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Clearly. Let's just bake. I'll measure. You watch.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Watch? I'm not a child.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I didn't say you were. I said watch so you don't interrupt.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: That's condescending.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's practical. Every time you participate, you misread my pauses.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Maybe if you didn't pause so much, I wouldn't misread.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Maybe if you didn't assume every pause was an ending, we wouldn't have this problem.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: We're going in circles.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Because you won't accept that you're interrupting.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: And you won't accept that your delivery is unclear.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: My delivery is fine. You just don't understand when I'm done.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Exactly. I don't understand. Because you don't signal clearly.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I held up a card. I said 'reading now.' What more do you want?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I want you to speak in complete thoughts without long pauses.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I can't read a recipe without pauses. I need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Then say 'looking at recipe' instead of going silent.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Okay. Looking at recipe. Silence means looking.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Silence means done to me. We have different languages.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Then we need to learn each other's language.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I'm trying. But you keep getting angry.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm not angry. I'm correcting you.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Correction feels like anger.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: What should I do then? Let you keep adding wrong ingredients?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You could say it gently.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I have been gentle. For twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Twenty minutes of gentle correction still feels like criticism.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm criticizing the behavior, not you.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It feels like the same thing.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Okay. Let's restart. No criticism. Just baking.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Good. I like that.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Flour. Two cups. Sifted. Please sift into this bowl.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Sifting. Like this?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Yes. Perfect. Now sugar. One cup.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: One cup sugar. Adding.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Cocoa powder. One tablespoon.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: One tablespoon. Seems little, but okay.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Baking powder. One teaspoon.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: One teaspoon. Got it.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Salt. Half a teaspoon.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Half teaspoon salt. In it goes.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Good. Now whisk the dry ingredients.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Whisking. This is better. Clear steps.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Yes. Now wet ingredients. Buttermilk. One cup.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: One cup buttermilk. Pouring.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Two eggs.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Cracking. One. Two.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Butter. Half cup. Melted.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Melting butter now.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Vanilla. One teaspoon.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Vanilla in.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Red food coloring. Two tablespoons.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Two tablespoons? That's so much.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I know. But that's the recipe.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It looks like blood.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's supposed to look red. Hence red velvet.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I know, but this much dye seems unhealthy.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's food-safe. Can we just follow the recipe?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Fine. Adding it.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Now mix the wet ingredients.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Mixing. Very red.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Now fold the wet into the dry. Gently.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Folding. Like this?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Yes. Don't overmix.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It makes the cake tough. Gluten develops.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I see. Being gentle.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Good. Now pour into the pans.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Pans are ready. Pouring.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Evenly. Split between two.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Half and half. Done.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Into the oven. 350 degrees. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Setting timer. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Good. Now we wait.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: So, tell me about school.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: School is fine. I'm taking a film class.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Film! That's why you're so particular about timing.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: No, I'm particular about timing because you keep interrupting.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: There you go again. Criticizing.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Stating facts. We just had a system that worked.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: And now we're chatting. Different system.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Chatting shouldn't mean overlapping either.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You want me to be silent during chat time too?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: No. I want natural turn-taking.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: My natural is overlapping.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Then your natural causes misunderstandings.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Only because you interpret them as attacks.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I don't interpret them as attacks. I interpret them as not listening.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I am listening. I just respond quickly.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Before I've finished my thought.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Your thoughts are long. I have thoughts too.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Then wait your turn.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I feel like I'm in school.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm not trying to school you. I'm trying to communicate.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It feels like lecturing.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Because you won't acknowledge the problem.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I acknowledge that we have different styles.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Different styles that don't work together.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: They worked fine when you were little.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: When I was little, I didn't need precise instructions.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: And now you do. Everything has to be precise.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Baking requires precision.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Baking also requires love. And patience.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I have patience. I've been patient for an hour.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: An hour of patience that looks like frustration.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The timer! Is the cake done?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I'll check.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Use the mitts!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I know! I'm not stupid.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I didn't say you were stupid. I said use the mitts.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You say it like I don't know.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Because you reached without them.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I was just touching the oven door.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The mitts should be on before you approach the oven.
